headline: DAME 🏆 ESTHER Rantzen DIES 💀 at 86 After LEGENDARY 📺 Run
text:
VETERAN 📻 broadcaster DAME 👑 Esther Rantzen has DIED 💀 at the age of 86 🕯️ after a lifetime 🧬 of changing 📈 countless lives through her iconic 🏆 BBC show That's Life! for 21 years 🗓️ and founding 🏗️ the absolute LIFESAVER ❤️ Childline in 1986 🛟 plus Silver Line 🧓 for lonely elders later on 🌅. She went full 🏃‍♀️ campaigner mode for assisted dying laws ⚖️ even while terminally ill 🤒 with lung cancer 🫁 and joined Dignitas 🏥 in December 2023 📆 but ended up too physically fragile 🦵 to make the trip ✈️ despite spending the money 💸 and making all the plans 📋. Prime Minister Andy Burnham praised her for having "changed countless lives" 🫂 while her family called her the most wonderful mother 👩‍❤️‍👩 and cherished grandmother 👵 whose compassion lives on through her charities forever ♾️. In her final statement 📝 she begged the law must "change and change quickly" 🏎️ ahead of that Terminally Ill Adults Bill which sadly failed 🚫 to pass the Commons 🏛️ leaving her deeply sad 😔 that it won't come soon enough for so many who need it 🕊️.

Dame Esther absolutely COOKED 🍳 on That's Life! from 1973 to 1994 🕰️ pulling in 20 million viewers 📺 every week with a wild mix of serious consumer investigations 🔎 and light-hearted items like talking dogs 🐶 Jobsworth Awards 🏅 and massive campaigns for abused children 🛡️ organ transplants ❤️ safe playgrounds 🛝 and justice for everyday consumers 🛒. Her most viewed episode ever 🌟 featured Sir Nicholas Winton getting the surprise of his life 😲 when she introduced him to Holocaust survivors he had saved ✡️ during that 1988 instalment 🎥 which still hits different even now 🥹. She started her journey as a BBC radio sound effects assistant 🔊 then became a TV researcher 🔬 trained as producer and director 🎬 and rose up from Bernard Braden's consumer show 📋 to become the formidable fun-loving face of That's Life! 🦸‍♀️. Later she popped up on Strictly Come Dancing 💃 First Dates ❤️ and I'm a Celebrity Get Me Out of Here! 🪳 showing that same spark that made her a true pioneer 🧭.

The absolute QUEEN 👸 of compassion revealed her lung cancer diagnosis in January 2023 🩺 saying it made her pour out "profound thanks to everyone who has made my life so joyful" 🌈 and even though she was down bad with the illness 🛌 she kept fighting for assisted dying rights 🗳️ right until the very end 🌅. In December 2024 she felt "great relief" 😌 after MPs backed the proposals to legalise assisted dying in England and Wales 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿 before it all stalled in the House of Lords 🏛️ and she told the Sunday Times she would "die happy" ☺️ as long as others could ask for help to die as they choose in the future ⏳. Her family announced her passing on Wednesday 🕯️ paying tribute to her humour 😂 ingenuity 🧠 and audacity 💥 that she brought to every single project and they hope it keeps inspiring all of us forever 🔥.

From her early days as a researcher and reporter 📝 on Braden's Week through to launching Childline which helped millions of kids 🧒 and Silver Line for isolated elderly folks 👴 she never stopped pushing boundaries 🏁. That iconic That's Life! moment with Nicholas Winton still gives everyone chills ❄️ and her website lists all the legendary bits like talking dogs 🐕 campaigns against abuse 🚫 and calls for better organ transplants 🫀 and safe playgrounds 🛝. She was married to documentary film-maker Desmond Wilcox 💍 from 1977 until he passed in 2000 and they raised three beautiful children 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 before she was made a dame in 2015 for services to children and older people 🏅. Figures from politics 🏛️ broadcasting 📡 and charity sector all lined up to pay tribute calling her a legend of British broadcasting 📻 whose warmth spirit and fight for justice changed millions of lives across decades 🕰️.

BBC director-general Matt Brittin called her contribution to public life "immeasurable" 📏 while money saving expert Martin Lewis labelled her an "inspiration" and "pioneer" whose impact will keep shining bright ✨. Kim Leadbeater the Labour MP who sponsored the assisted dying bill described Dame Esther as a wonderful mix of strength 💪 feistiness 🔥 deep compassion ❤️ and kindness 🕊️ saying she will continue to inspire campaigners everywhere 🌍. Chris Sherwood from the NSPCC which now runs Childline praised how she went to exceptional lengths 🏋️ to give children and young people somewhere safe to turn when they needed help 🆘. Her co-presenter Bill Buckley said on Radio 4 that "nothing would stop her" when campaigning 🏃‍♀️ as she saw the light at the end of the tunnel and followed it doggedly 🕯️. Anton Du Beke shared their Strictly dancing photo 🕺 calling her the ultimate breaker of the glass ceiling 🪟 and Davina McCall posted that she "made the world a better place" 🌎 inspiring girls like her to live life to the fullest 🥳. Amol Rajan summed it up perfectly by saying she "changed the course of millions of lives" as an inspirational strong woman ahead of her time born in Hertfordshire during early WWII 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 and that is one hell of a legacy to leave behind 👏.
